subject: Observability transport validation & SIEM onboarding for Meridian Health
messages:
From: Michael Lawson <michael.lawson@meridianhealth.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@meridianhealth.com
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: SIEM onboarding + log/trace export for VPC private deployment

Hi Connor,

Thanks for taking this — Meridian is getting close to signing the PO for a Private deployment (VPC) and security asked me to get visibility into how logs and traces will be exported to our Splunk Cloud instance. Attached is our onboarding checklist and a rough network diagram.

Key asks from security:
- Confirm what ports/protocols the forwarder needs to reach Splunk HEC (we prefer egress-only, TLS).
- Token lifecycle and rotation guidance for HEC tokens + how Redwood stores/secrets management.
- Trace sampling hook: can we forward trace spans (OTLP) to our collector in parallel to the platform traces?
- Guidance on evidence bundles for audits (time windows, formats).

Can you outline an operational plan and a minimal runbook (network, firewall rules, certs, fallback) we can include in the security package? We plan to start the environment build next week, so a quick validation would be ideal.

Appreciate it — feel free to loop in any infra/observability engineers.

Thanks,
Michael Lawson
Lead Security Engineer
Meridian Health
attachments: Meridian_SIEM_Onboarding_Req.pdf, meridian-network-diagram-v1.png
From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Lawson <michael.lawson@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM onboarding + log/trace export for VPC private deployment

Michael — thanks for the checklist and diagram. Looping in Karthik (onprem runtime) and Kimberly (security/compliance) to validate specifics.

High-level plan (short summary):
1) Egress connector: deploy a lightweight forwarder inside your VPC that ships logs/metrics/traces out to Splunk HEC over TLS 443. We recommend using a hardened forwarder with mutual TLS when customer policy requires two-way certs; otherwise HEC token + TLS is sufficient.
2) Ports: outbound 443 to the HEC endpoint + 443 to our telemetry-control plane for health checks (optional, can be routed via customer proxy).
3) Secrets: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for HEC tokens and forwarder certs. We do not persist raw tokens in plaintext; tokens are stored encrypted and rotated via recommended policies (we'll provide rotation playbook).
4) Tracing: we can mirror OTLP spans to your collector in parallel to our internal tracing pipeline. We will include a sampling map to avoid double-counting and to preserve PII redaction rules.
5) Evidence bundles: per-audit bundles generated from our private telemetry exporter (JSON logs + gzipped trace snippets), retention windows configurable; standard bundle includes 30 days of logs and a 72-hour trace window by default.

Action items for us: Karthik, can you validate ports and forwarder footprint? Kimberly, please confirm the rotation playbook & token handling language for the security packet. Marissa, can you own the runbook doc and a short timeline for completion?

We can do a 30-minute call Monday to walk through the plan and capture any policy blockers. Proposed times: Mon 6/8 9am PT or 11am PT.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Lawson <michael.lawson@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIEM onboarding + log/trace export for VPC private deployment

Thanks — quick technical validation from my side:

Forwarder options (supported):
- Splunk HEC agent (recommended): outbound HTTPS (443) to HEC endpoint. Accepts HEC token in header.
- OpenTelemetry Collector: supports OTLP/HTTP (443) for traces and can forward logs/metrics to HEC via HEC exporter.
- Syslog forwarder over TLS (6514) if your Splunk environment prefers syslog ingest — we can support that but it requires inbound rules on your side for the forwarder to push.

Network / Ports (minimal):
- outbound TCP 443 to <splunk-hec-host>:443 (HEC ingestion)
- outbound TCP 443 to telemetry.redwood.internal (control plane health checks) — optional; can be proxied through your egress.
- if using syslog over TLS: outbound TCP 6514 (client syslog over TLS).

Security:
- HEC tokens: provide rotated HEC token(s). We recommend short-lived tokens (30d) and a token rotation window with two active tokens for graceful swap.
- Secrets storage: we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for private deployments; tokens are encrypted with CMEK.
- Certificate pinning: where mutual TLS is required we can provide CSR flow and accept customer-signed certs for the forwarder.

Trace behavior:
- We'll deploy an OTEL shim alongside the forwarder to mirror spans. Default sampling: 0.5% global with route-based overrides for high-priority endpoints. Spans forwarded to your OTLP endpoint will be PII-scrubbed per the config provided in the security packet.

Evidence bundles / audit:
- Bundle format: gzipped tar with JSON logs (ndjson), OTLP trace snippets (protobuf wrapped/JSON), and an index manifest.
- Delivery: SFTP or secure presigned URL to your artifact store.
- Retention: can snapshot daily; standard retention policy in our private deployments is 90 days, but audit exports are configurable per contract.

Attachments: small example forwarder config (redwood-onprem-forwarder-config.example).

Connor — I can draft a minimal firewall rule list and a 1-page runbook we can attach to the security packet.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

- Our Splunk team prefers HEC over OTLP for ingestion; we'll provide HEC endpoint + initial token by EOD Monday.
- For evidence transfer, SFTP is our preferred channel; can you confirm retention export cadence (daily snapshot OK)?
- For mutual TLS, our security leads will review the CSR flow — please add a short checklist for cert rotation to the runbook.

We can do the call Mon 6/8 at 11am PT. Please send calendar invite and a draft of the 1-page runbook before the call if possible.

Thanks — Michael
